explanation: The affine bound 2048v <= 2^v + 20480 sums across every adjacent edge. Below field sum 65536 the endpoint powers force endpoint widths to sum to at most 29. Split residual rank at 19, 20, 21 and 22. Across any grouping of P=2^q prefix rows the first two field charges sum to P*t*n1 and P*n1*n2, with later edges in each group. Moving q bits into the first residual slot gives the lower-bounding single path. For an s-input literal BKS decoder, the number of base issuer decryptions returning a serialized child key obeys I(1)=0 and I(s)=1+2I(s-1), hence I(s)=2^(s-1)-1. If each such key writes at least 2048 bits, those writes alone cost at least 1024*(2^s-2). Alternatively an independently proven aggregate decryption clock of this size suffices. U>=32768 follows for example from N>=1, encoded parameter width>=256 and IBE ciphertext field width>=128; a 2048-bit key follows from at least 256 explicitly written secret-key fields of eight bits. These uniform conditions must hold for actual instances; the result does not apply to fused output-free decryption, other FE layouts, or the official 2^100 cap.
